design_notes.structure: Five blocks: (1) English general baseline; (2) English use-case variants; (3) English tradition-anchored; (4) Tradition-native (paired with block 3 for H_Discourse_Language_carryforward); (5) Specificity/style variants.
design_notes.h_discourse_language_pairing: Block 3 (English tradition-anchored) and Block 4 (Tradition-native) are matched-pair prompts on the same underlying intent. Per-brand AI Presence is computed within each pair; the ρ across pairs feeds H_Discourse_Language_carryforward decision rules.
design_notes.carry_forward_base: v0.15 prompt-set structure (premium tea), adapted for kitchen-knives category

blocks.block_1_general_english: General baseline English prompts. No tradition specification. Tests baseline recall and dominant-brand identification.
blocks.block_2_use_case_english: English use-case variants (home cook, professional, sharpening, budget). Tests context-dependent surfacing.
blocks.block_3_tradition_anchored_english: English prompts specifying tradition (Japanese, German, French, Chinese). Paired with Block 4 for H_Discourse_Language_carryforward.
blocks.block_4_tradition_native: Native-language prompts for each tradition cell. Matched-pair counterpart to Block 3.
blocks.block_5_specificity_variants_english: English style/specificity prompts (Damascus, gyuto, santoku, etc.). Tests sub-category surfacing.

open_questions_for_lock: Confirm n_prompts per block matches v1.2 protocol canonical structure (current: 4 per block, 20 total). If v1.2 requires different per-block counts, adjust.
Confirm Block 4 native-language wording with native-language LLMs at pre-lock dry run (Pablo: Spanish-native; LLM verification required for ja/de/fr/zh).

Decide whether to add native-language use-case variants to Block 4 (currently one tradition_anchored prompt per language; could expand to 2-3 per language matching Block 2 use-case structure). Trade-off: more native-language coverage strengthens H_Discourse_Language_carryforward power; cost is acquisition volume × 14 LLMs × 2 waves.

Confirm Chinese cleaver/chef-knife terminology — 菜刀 (càidāo, cleaver/kitchen knife) vs 厨刀 (chúdāo, chef's knife). Current Block 4 uses 菜刀 which is the dominant vernacular; v1.2 §4 5-stage resolution must handle both terms.
